# copick match pytom-extract

<span class="source-badge source-badge--pytom-match" title="Provided by the copick-pytom-match plugin">pytom-match</span>

*Extract particles again from score maps stored by 'copick match pytom --maps'.*

??? info "Plugin command — copick-pytom-match"
    This command is provided by the **[copick-pytom-match](https://github.com/copick/copick-pytom)** plugin, not copick core. Install it to make this command available:

    ```bash
    pip install git+https://github.com/copick/copick-pytom.git
    # pytom-match-pick in its own environment, e.g.:
    conda create -n pytom -c conda-forge python=3.12 cupy cuda-version=12.6
    conda run -n pytom pip install "pytom-match-pick==0.14.*"
    ```

    See the [plugin system](../index.md#plugin-system) guide for details.

## Usage

```bash
copick match pytom-extract [OPTIONS]
```

## Description

Matching is the expensive step; extraction only reads the score and angle maps. With the maps stored in copick,
the extraction settings (number of particles, cut-off, peak spacing, tophat filter, mask) can be changed and the
particles extracted again without matching. pytom's job is rebuilt in a scratch directory from the record stored
with the maps, pytom_extract_candidates.py runs, and the particles become copick picks.

## URI Format

```text
Tomograms:     type@voxel_spacing
Picks:         object_name:user_id/session_id
Segmentations: name:user_id/session_id@voxel_spacing
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `-c, --config` | path | — | Path to the configuration file. |
| `--maps` | text | **required** | The stored score map, as a tomogram URI type@voxel_size (its angles are in type-angles). |
| `--run-names, -r` | text · multiple | — | Specific run names to process (default: all runs). Repeatable; pass -r once per run. |
| `--output, -o` | text | **required** | Picks URI, object[:user[/session]]; the object must be in the configuration. [default user/session: pytom/1] |
| `--number-of-particles, -n` | integer range | `1000` | The most particles to extract per tomogram. |
| `--cut-off` | float range | — | Extract down to this LCCmax instead of the estimated false-alarm cut-off. |
| `--number-of-false-positives` | float range | `1.0` | Tolerated false positives of the estimated cut-off; higher extracts more. |
| `--extraction-diameter` | float range | — | Peaks closer than half this (Angstrom) are suppressed. [default: the particle diameter] |
| `--tophat-filter` | boolean flag | `False` | Keep only sharp peaks (tophat transform). |
| `--tophat-connectivity` | integer range | `1` | Connectivity of the tophat transform. |
| `--tophat-bins` | integer range | `50` | Histogram bins of the tophat cut-off estimate. |
| `--ignore-tomogram-mask` | boolean flag | `False` | Extract outside the tomogram mask too. |
| `--tomogram-mask` | text | — | Segmentation URI of an extraction mask. [default: the mask the job matched with, if any] |
| `--angular-search` | file | — | The custom angle file the job matched with; needed only when it used one. |
| `--max-workers` | integer range | `4` | Runs extracted at once. |
| `--scratch-dir` | directory | — | Where the temporary job files go; they are always removed. [default: the system temp dir] |
| `--pytom-bin-dir` | directory | — | Directory with pytom-match-pick's scripts. [default: PATH] |
| `--report` | file | — | Write a JSON report of every run here. |
| `--overwrite / --no-overwrite` | boolean flag | `False` | Replace existing outputs; without it, runs that have them are skipped. |
| `--debug / --no-debug` | boolean flag | `False` | Enable debug logging. |

## Examples

```bash
# A stricter cut-off into a new session
copick match pytom-extract -c config.json --maps ribosome-scores@10.0 -o ribosome:pytom/2 --cut-off 0.25

# Only inside a lamella segmentation, with sharp peaks
copick match pytom-extract -c config.json --maps ribosome-scores@10.0 -o ribosome:pytom/3 \
    --tomogram-mask lamella:membrain/1 --tophat-filter
```

## See also

- [`copick match pytom`](pytom.md) — template matching that stores the maps (--maps)

## Notes

Needs no GPU, but runs pytom-match-pick's script from its environment (--pytom-bin-dir).
The exit status is non-zero when a run fails.
